title: Such a helpful friend
odia:
ଉପକାରିଆ ବନ୍ଧୁ
ଆମ୍ବ ଆଣି ନାହିଁ, ଶିମ୍ବ ଆଣିନାହିଁ
ଆଣିଚି କଷା କେନ୍ଦୁ।
literal_meaning: A helpful friend: they brought no mangoes, brought no beans; they brought astringent kendu fruit.
meaning_odia: ବନ୍ଧୁକୁ ଉପକାରିଆ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେ ଆମ୍ବ ବା ଶିମ୍ବ ବଦଳରେ କଷା କେନ୍ଦୁ ଆଣିଛି। ଆଶା ମୁତାବକ ଉପକାର ନମିଳିବାରୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସାଟି ଏଠାରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୋଇଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The opening calls the friend helpful, then the gift undercuts the praise. Mangoes and beans are named as the things not brought; the final line leaves the speaker with astringent kendu instead. This edition reads the mismatch as irony about a favour that disappoints its recipient.
usage_example: A friend offers to bring something useful for a shared meal, but arrives with something the group cannot use as hoped. Someone might recall these lines with a teasing “such a helpful friend.” This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The three foods give the complaint a concrete shape. କଷା specifies the astringent, mouth-puckering taste of the offered fruit, sharpening the contrast with the opening praise. The humour lies in the disappointed speaker’s evaluation of this gift.

graphic.caption: An imagined gift meets a response less grateful than its giver expects.
